descriptionChirho: To make oneself warm, typically by sitting or standing near a fire; used in both middle-reflexive (warming oneself) and passive-imperative (be warmed) voice. All occurrences cluster around the same physical action of seeking warmth. Translations are consistent: 'warming himself / be warmed' (eng), 'calentandose / calentaos' (spa), 'akiota moto / mkiota moto' (swa: warming at fire), 'taap raha tha / garm ho' (hin: warming / become warm), 'yastadfi'u / istadfi'uu' (arb: warming oneself), 'bul jjolgo' (kor: warming by fire). The imperative 'be warmed' (S69184, James 2:16) and imperfect plural (S69185) are grammatical variants, not different senses.
